speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by pinpointing the onset: when did your double vision and upper limb weakness first appear, and have they been getting worse? Additionally, do you experience any trouble swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is classic for myasthenia gravis; however, your description of double vision specifically when looking up or down also strongly suggests a specific cranial nerve palsy. Given your age and symptoms, do you have a history of smoking or exposure to asbestos? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to check for a lung mass or mediastinal widening.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal chest X-ray, we can rule out a tumor pressing on the nerves. I need to know if your symptoms fluctuate significantly throughout the day or if you experience drooping eyelids (ptosis) when you try to focus? Also, do you have any known autoimmune diseases or take any medications that might weaken muscles? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness, ocular symptoms triggered by specific eye movements, and the positive acetylcholine receptor antibody test confirms this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. Do you notice your eyelids drooping more at the end of the day?
